about: REAL dispensing figures for England behind anumaan/realcheck.py: items and quantity per integrated care board (ICB) per month. Rows of index_items, index_qty and substitute_items are ICBs in sorted code order (the keys of regions); columns are the study's months. index_qty is in the study's unit. A study's substance, notice, index and substitutes say what to fetch: notice is the month of the first official notice (a placebo borrows its shortage's); index maps the last two characters of a BNF code, which the brand, the generic name and imported packs of one presentation share, to units per unit dispensed; substitutes is a pattern on the names of the substance's other products, and the rest are counted in neither (other_names). notices are official; earlier_reports are press and charity reports from before the first of them. The figures, the name lists, months, regions, fetched and query are rewritten by: python -m anumaan.realcheck --fetch

source.publisher: NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) Open Data Portal
source.attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
source.note: Prescriptions issued in England and dispensed in the community, per GP practice and product; one table a month, EPD_YYYYMM. The portal now marks this dataset retired: it stops at June 2025 and 'EPD with SNOMED code' carries on. Every month used here is in it.

query: SELECT {area} AS icb, REGIONAL_OFFICE_CODE AS region, BNF_CODE AS code, BNF_DESCRIPTION AS name, SUM(ITEMS) AS items, SUM(TOTAL_QUANTITY) AS qty FROM `{table}` WHERE BNF_CHEMICAL_SUBSTANCE = '{substance}' GROUP BY icb, region, code, name
caveats: Premise only. This asks whether rationing and substitution leave marks in routine dispensing records, in many districts at once, when a shortage is officially declared. Anumaan's filter never runs here, and English community pharmacies are not Indian primary health centres.

Monthly totals per ICB, not patient records: 'cut short' is a fall in the average quantity per item and 'substituting' is a rise in other products' share of items. Neither is a switch seen in one patient's course.

A fingerprint that a notice ordered is not early warning. The February 2024 Creon notice asked for one month's supply at most and for 10,000-unit capsules in place of 25,000; from 19 May 2022 a protocol let pharmacists supply patches for Oestrogel. Flags in those months are partly the notices' own doing.

The 12 months before each first notice were not shortage-free (see earlier_reports). Creon's maker reported a supply constraint on Creon 25000 on 19 September 2023, and Oestrogel's maker had reported shortages by 12 April 2022. The wide rule fired in those baselines in September and November 2023 (Creon) and in February and March 2022 (Oestrogel). These may be early signals rather than false flags; this check cannot tell which, so read the two shortages' no-shortage figures as an upper bound on false flags.

Thresholds were fixed before the data was looked at and not tuned, but results lean on them. The fixed baseline has no trend term, so a slow drift ends up flagged: azathioprine's tablets per item fell 3.6% over its 2023-25 window and met the wide rule in its last month. Creon is the most sensitive. With double the MAD floor its substitution peak is 11 ICBs, not 28, the wide rule is first met in April 2024, and 'cut short' no longer meets it after the notice. With half the floor the peak is 37, but the azathioprine placebo then meets the wide rule six times, not once. Oestrogel's substitution result barely moves.

Creon quantity is counted in 25,000-unit capsules (a 10,000-unit capsule counts 0.4), because the first notice asked prescribers to swap strengths. Counted in plain capsules, the dips of September 2023 and February 2024 vanish (more, weaker capsules per item) and the wide rule is met only in August and September 2024, by 4 and 5 ICBs.

Index products include the generic name and imported packs of the same presentation. Every other pancreatin product counts as a Creon substitute, Creon Micro granules and Creon 40000 included. For estradiol the substitutes are the other skin products (patches, gel sachets, spray), several of which had shortage protocols of their own in 2021-23; tablets and implants are left out.

Areas: the dataset names them STP_CODE up to April 2022 and ICB_CODE after, with the same 42 codes. Between June and July 2022 the item counts of five areas step by 5-20% (QF7, QT1, QHL, QUA, QJ2): practices changed area when ICBs were set up on 1 July 2022. The ratios used here move far less. Practices the dataset could not place (area '-') are left out: a few items a month.

Placebos: neither amlodipine nor azathioprine tablets has had a Serious Shortage Protocol or a National Patient Safety Alert. Lesser supply notices cannot be ruled out, because the official Medicines Supply Tool needs a login. Two shortages and two placebo medicines, picked by hand, are an illustration, not a validation.

studies.name: Creon capsules (pancreatic enzymes), 2024

notices.text: Medicine Supply Notification MSN/2024/022 (DHSC and NHS England, tier 2): Creon 25,000 capsules are out of stock until late February 2024; prescribe Creon 10,000 capsules to make up the dose, one month's supply at most. The first official notice found. Read from a copy of the notification hosted by the Dispensing Doctors' Association: the official Medicines Supply Tool needs a login.

Medicine Supply Notification MSN/2024/054 (tier 2): Creon 10,000 and 25,000 capsules in limited supply until 2026, Nutrizym 22 out of stock until mid-August 2024, Pancrex V unable to support more demand; prescribe one month's supply at most. The alert of 24 May confirms its date; the text was read from a copy hosted by Community Pharmacy South Central.

National Patient Safety Alert NatPSA/2024/007/DHSC, 'Shortage of Pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT)': prescribe one month's supply at most; pharmacists to supply one month in line with SSP060 and SSP061.

Serious Shortage Protocols SSP060 (Creon 10000 capsules) and SSP061 (Creon 25000 capsules): a pharmacist may cut a prescription for more than one month to one month's supply. Valid from 24 May 2024 and extended since (to 2 October 2026 when read on 30 September 2026).
National Patient Safety Alert NatPSA/2024/013/DHSC, additional actions: Creon capsules still in limited supply until 2026; Nutrizym 22 and Pancrex V only intermittently available.

earlier_reports.text: Neuroendocrine Cancer UK: members report being unable to get Creon prescriptions filled; the maker expects deliveries that week. A charity's report, not an official notice.

Neuroendocrine Cancer UK, relaying Creon's maker Viatris: 'a temporary supply constraint of Creon 25000u capsules', so wholesalers and pharmacies may be out of stock; next UK delivery 22 September. Not an official notice.

substitute_names: Gen Creon Micro Pancreatin 60.12mg gastro-resistant granules
Generic Pancrex V oral powder sugar free

notices.text: Serious Shortage Protocol SSP019, Oestrogel Pump-Pack 0.06% gel: a pharmacist may cut a prescription for more than three months to three months' supply. Valid from 29 April 2022 (to 30 November 2022 after extensions). The first official notice found.

DHSC press release 'Three-month limit for 3 HRT products to ensure continued access': protocols issued for Oestrogel, Ovestin cream and Premique Low Dose, to even out demand for products 'which have recently experienced issues due to rising demand'.

Medicine Supply Notification MSN/2022/037 for Oestrogel (tier 2). Not seen itself: its update of 23 May 2022, MSN/2022/037-U, calls itself an 'update to communication issued 3 May 2022'; read from a copy hosted by NHS Bath and North East Somerset, Swindon and Wiltshire ICB.

Serious Shortage Protocols SSP022 and SSP023, Oestrogel: where it is unavailable a pharmacist may supply estradiol patches instead (Evorel, Estraderm MX, FemSeven, Progynova TS). Valid from 19 May 2022 on the NHSBSA list and in the protocol; the supply notification says issued 20 May.

DHSC press release 'Further action taken to improve supply of HRT': further protocols let pharmacists substitute Oestrogel, Ovestin cream, Lenzetto spray and Sandrena gel with alternatives such as patches.

earlier_reports.text: GP Online: Oestrogel's maker Besins Healthcare reports 'exceptionally high demand' for Oestrogel 'in recent months, resulting in shortages of the product'. A press report, not an official notice.
